summary: States that the IPv6 address space will be managed by the IANA for the good of the Internet community, with advice from the IAB and IESG, by delegation to the regional registries. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Who hands out the Internet's next generation of addresses: one central office lends them out to regional offices.

questions: how does ipv6 address allocation work
what is the regional internet registry
subtitle: Who will hand out the next generation of Internet addresses

tldr.problem: As IPv6 deployment approached, the Internet community needed to decide who would manage and allocate the vastly larger IPv6 address space.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1881 establishes that IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority) manages the IPv6 address space on behalf of the Internet, with advice from the IAB and IESG, by delegating to regional registries that make the actual allocations to service providers and organizations.
tldr.outcome: A clear management hierarchy ensures orderly allocation, prevents conflicts, and allows delegation so one authority need not handle every allocation request worldwide.

today: RFC 1881 is Informational and describes the management structure that has operated since 1995. The IANA, regional registries, and delegation model it describes remain in use today for IPv6 allocation.

sections.title: Why IPv6 Needs Centralized Management
sections.content:
IPv6 introduces 128-bit addresses, enough for every star in the universe to have a billion Internets. With such a huge space, the Internet community recognized that some central authority must oversee allocation to prevent conflicts and ensure fair distribution. That authority is IANA.

IANA does not make every allocation itself. Instead, it delegates responsibility to regional registries (such as RIPE, APNIC, and ARIN) that are closer to end-users and service providers, and those regional registries make allocations in their regions.
sections.eli5: With so many addresses available, you still need one person to say who gets which big block, then let regional offices give out smaller chunks.

sections.title: Principles for Address Management
sections.content:
RFC 1881 states that IPv6 addresses MUST be managed for the good of the Internet community. IANA relies on advice from the IAB (Internet Architecture Board) and IESG (Internet Engineering Steering Group) when making allocation decisions.

The document also establishes that if a regional registry mishandles its delegated space, IANA may revoke the delegation after due notice. Revenue from address space (if any) goes only to cover registry costs, not to subsidize other activities. And monopoly control or predatory practices must be avoided.
sections.eli5: An office gets a block of addresses and is supposed to be fair about giving them out. If it acts unfairly or wastes the addresses, the central office can take the block back.

sections.title: What This Establishes
sections.content:
RFC 1881 declares that individuals and organizations may obtain IPv6 address allocations directly from their regional registry or through a service provider. It commits IANA to developing a plan for initial allocation and procedures for appeals if an allocation is denied.

This informational RFC does not define specific allocation policies, block sizes, or technical procedures; those details were developed in separate standards documents that follow IANA's guidance.
sections.eli5: Organizations know now that they can ask for addresses from a regional office near them, and there's a fair process if something goes wrong.
